Since the first case last month, the prefecture reports ongoing domestic transmission, indicating local spread. Public health authorities urge anyone with suspected measles symptoms to call ahead to medical facilities and follow instructions when seeking care.

articles.headlineTranslated: One more measles case: a woman in her 40s from Toyama who had contact with an infected person
articles.summary: Measles case reported in Toyama: a woman in her 40s in Toyama City contracted measles after contact with a man in his 20s whose infection was confirmed on the 12th. The patient developed fever on the 25th and sought medical care on the 26th; laboratory confirmation was reported by the prefectural Public Health Institute. She is currently convalescing at home. She has received one measles vaccination dose and had no recent overseas travel. This year, five measles cases have been identified in the prefecture. Japan was declared to be in an elimination state for endemic measles in 2015, but imports linked to travelers have driven recent outbreaks; authorities warn the virus is highly contagious and not fully preventable by handwashing or masks, and urge vaccination to prevent further spread.

articles.headlineTranslated: Two new measles patients confirmed in Toyama Prefecture, the fourth case this month; prefecture urges caution (June 25, 2026) | KNB NEWS NNN
articles.summary: Two new measles cases have been confirmed in Toyama Prefecture's Takaoka City, the fourth measles case this month and prompting a prefectural warning. The patients are a man in his 20s and a woman in her 40s, residents within the Takaoka Health Center jurisdiction, and both were contacts of the measles patient announced on June 12. Health authorities conducted exposure monitoring, and fever was detected on June 23 during health observations. The prefecture’s Public Health Laboratory confirmed measles infection through genetic testing. Measles is highly contagious, with transmission possible from mere co-location. The prefecture urges anyone showing suspected symptoms to contact a medical facility by phone in advance and to follow staff instructions when seeking care. The ongoing month-long cluster underscores heightened vigilance in Toyama.

articles.headlineTranslated: Japan-developed Nipah virus vaccine for a high-fatality Nipah virus begins clinical trials in Belgium
articles.summary: Japan-developed Nipah virus vaccine, using a live-attenuated measles virus vector carrying Nipah genes, began clinical trials in Belgium on June 15, testing safety and immunogenicity in 60 healthy adults. Nipah virus, transmitted from fruit bats to people (and occasionally via human contact), can cause fever and myalgia and may progress to encephalitis with high fatality; there are no approved treatments or vaccines. The vaccine showed safety and efficacy in animal studies. If safety and immune response are confirmed, trials are planned in Bangladesh, where Nipah outbreaks occur. The project is led by Misako Yoneda of Teikyo University, with collaborators including the European Vaccine Initiative, Stanford University, and Japan’s Center for Advanced Research and Development Strategy. Researchers describe this as a potential step toward a practical vaccine against a deadly, zoonotic infection.

Nationwide measles transmission is reported, with Kumamoto City Public Health Center noting no current evidence of broader spread. On June 1, it was learned that a person who had contact with the patient outside the prefecture had developed measles by June 3. Public health authorities state the infection does not appear to be expanding at present. Vaccination remains the most effective prevention against measles.

articles.headlineTranslated: Measles spreading in the Tokyo metropolitan area and urban Kansai areas: a quick refresher on what kind of disease it is.
articles.summary: Measles is spreading in the Tokyo metropolitan area and urban Kansai areas, likely surpassing the 2019 peak. Those in their late teens to 30s form the outbreak core, with immunity lower among this group than among 50s+ who had natural exposure, making measles a concern for young adults as well as children. After a 10–12 day incubation, patients develop fever (~38°C), cough, runny nose, and conjunctivitis; the catarrhal stage is the most contagious, with transmission risk near 100% for susceptible contacts and possible infection after a 30-minute room exposure. A subsequent fever spike (≥39°C) accompanies a characteristic red rash that starts on the neck or forehead and spreads to the body; pneumonia and encephalitis risk rise. Contagiousness persists for three days after fever subsides. Vaccination is the most reliable prevention: one dose is >95% effective; two doses are recommended. If immunity history is unknown, check with a blood test.

articles.summary: Measles cases in Japan this year reach 525, with two new nationwide infections reported in the week through June 7 (one in Chiba Prefecture and one in Gunma Prefecture). The cumulative total is about 3.9 times higher than the same period last year. Dr. Takeshi Terashima, a respiratory medicine specialist, notes measles spreads more easily at around 20°C, suggesting seasonal factors may slow the current rise. Nonetheless, infections commonly peak from spring to early summer, and increased international travel during summer vacations could boost case numbers. The Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare urges travelers to consider vaccination as appropriate before overseas trips.

articles.summary: As of June 14, 2026, measles outbreaks are expanding globally, with Japan reporting a rapid rise in 2026, particularly in the Kanto, Chubu, and Kansai regions. articles.summary: Measles infection reported in a man in his 20s residing in the Takaoka Public Health Center area of Toyama Prefecture, Japan. It is the first measles case in Toyama since November 2019 amid a domestic outbreak. The patient developed fever on the 3rd and visited a Toyama medical facility on the 12th; infection was confirmed by genetic testing at the prefectural Public Health Laboratory and he remains under treatment. He had traveled to Indonesia about three days before onset, an area with higher measles exposure risk. Measles presents with fever and cough and can lead to pneumonia, otitis media, or encephalitis; most patients recover within 7–10 days. Two scheduled routine vaccinations are administered at age 1 and before entering elementary school; authorities urge vaccination to prevent further spread.

Measles is highly contagious via airborne and droplet spread; in unimmunized individuals, illness begins with fever and cough, then a high fever (≥39°C) and rash lasting 4–5 days. The prefecture urges caution and advises contacting healthcare facilities by phone before visiting if measles is suspected.

Of the 11 new cases, Tokyo accounted for 7, Saitama 2, Kanagawa 1, and Ibaraki 1. No large-scale outbreak has been reported. Because measles is highly contagious, MOHLW urges continued vigilance, recommends checking vaccination status, and asks individuals with symptoms to contact a medical facility in advance.

articles.summary: Measles outbreak in Japan reports 511 provisional cases as of May 24, 2026, with Tokyo accounting for 253 cases (about half). The tally already exceeds last year’s total of 265 and is set to surpass the 2019 outbreak’s 744. Age distribution shows 20s 32%, 30s 21%, 15–19 14%, and 40s 11%, while those 50+ retain stronger immunity. Experts attribute the surge to reduced vaccination during the COVID-19 era and ongoing vaccine hesitancy, lowering population immunity. Measles can cause pneumonia and otitis media; encephalitis occurs in about 1 in 1,000 cases, with mortality rates similar to those in developed countries. The WHO warns of a global resurgence, noting the virus is highly contagious. In context, the article cites Bangladesh as experiencing substantial deaths, illustrating severe outcomes in lower-resource settings. Keywords: vaccination, outbreak, public health measures.

articles.summary: Measles cases in Japan reached 511 this year, the second-highest in the past decade, according to the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW). In the week ending May 24, 11 new cases were reported nationwide, with Tokyo accounting for 8 cases, followed by Aichi Prefecture (2) and Osaka (1). Measles is highly contagious, with nearly all susceptible individuals at risk; the incubation period is about 10 days, followed by cold-like symptoms, then high fever and a characteristic rash. Authorities urge verification of vaccination records and to contact a medical institution in advance if symptoms emerge. On June 1, MHLW launched a new national data system to consolidate individuals' vaccination histories and suspected adverse events via the My Number Portal, using anonymized data to assess vaccine effectiveness and safety. The government aims to aggregate nationwide information by spring 2028.

articles.headline: 命に関わる重篤な合併症リスクも......驚異的な感染力を持つ麻しん（はしか）のリスクと、取るべき対策法
articles.headlineTranslated: Life-threatening risk of severe complications as well... the measles, with its astonishing contagiousness, and the measures to be taken.
articles.summary: Measles is spreading rapidly in Japan and worldwide, driven by its exceptionally high transmissibility (R0 12–18) and airborne spread. A single unimmunized person can infect up to 18 others; in households, about 90% of susceptible contacts become infected. The illness begins with a catarrhal phase (1–4 days) of fever 38–39°C, runny nose, cough and conjunctivitis, followed by a high fever and widespread rash during the eruption phase. Complications include pneumonia and, in about 1 in 1,000 cases, encephalitis; long-term sequelae and SSPE can occur years later. In Japan, outbreaks have surged: 45 cases in 2024, 265 in 2025, and 462 cases by week 18 of 2026 (through May 3), concentrated in urban areas such as Tokyo and Aichi, affecting adults over 20. Vaccination coverage remains below 95% (first dose 92.7%, second dose 91.0% in 2024). An emergency vaccination program for contacts started May 18, 2026. MR vaccine (two doses) offers 97–99% protection; one dose 93–95%.
